title: feat(spec): an object declares its default row scope, defaultRowScope, the RLS policy shape without object
body:
Fixes #24338
Clause-②: yes

The spec half of ruling E′ on #24164 (ruling comment 6250748677, items 1 and 7). `ObjectSchema` gains one optional key, `defaultRowScope`: one row-level security policy, written like a permission set's `rowLevelSecurity` entry without `object`, which the declaring object implies. Nothing reads the key yet. Its reader is the collection-point card #24340, its writers are the declarations card #24341, and the ADR note is #24339. No object that exists today changes behaviour: at the base commit `b2e78701f7` the word `defaultRowScope` occurs nowhere in this tree, and nowhere in objectui at the `.objectui-sha` pin `0707b4ae37` (`git grep` exit 1 on both, against a `sharingModel` control that hits on both).

## The shape, and why it is built this way

| | `RowLevelSecurityPolicySchema` (contract unchanged) | `DefaultRowScopeSchema` (new, `@objectstack/spec/security`) |
|:--|:--|:--|
| members | `name`, `label`, `description`, `object`, `operation`, `using`, `check`, `positions`, `enabled`, plus the `priority` and `tags` tombstones | the same member instances, without `object`, `priority` and `tags` |
| cross-field rules | at least one of `using` / `check`; no `check` on a `select` or `delete` policy | the same function |
| near-miss aliases | `roles`/`role` to `positions`, `withcheck` to `check`, `condition`/`filter`/`where` to `using` | the same table |
| `object` | required | refused by name, with guidance: it is implied, delete it |
| surface name | "this RLS policy" | "this object's default row scope" |

- **Why not `.omit({ object: true })`.** zod 4.6.5 throws on it: `.omit() cannot be used on object schemas containing refinements` (measured with a probe; the policy schema carries a `.superRefine`). So the new schema is rebuilt from the same three parts, each shared by reference, not copied: the policy schema's own `shape` minus the left-out keys, the refinement (now the named function `refineRowLevelSecurityPolicy`), and the alias table (now the const `RLS_POLICY_ALIASES`).
- **Every rule that does not need `object` is kept.** Both rules read only `operation`, `using` and `check`. The schema has no `object`-dependent default and no `object` alias. The one place `object` still appears is the inherited `check` describe, which defines an "applicable" policy as one whose `object` matches; that text is shared, not forked.
- **Why the two tombstones are left out too.** `priority` and `tags` are `retiredKey()` tombstones and accept no value. Leaving them out changes nothing the schema accepts: both are still refused, as unknown keys. It also keeps their upgrade text, which is about the `rowLevelSecurity[]` path, off a surface that never had either key, and keeps two `[RETIRED]` rows out of a new authorable-surface entry. The input type is pinned at compile time as exactly the policy input type with `object`, `priority` and `tags` omitted.
- **`RowLevelSecurityPolicySchema` keeps its contract; only its source moved.** The inline `.superRefine` body moved into the named function verbatim (the 45 lines were compared by a script before the swap: identical), and the alias object moved into the const. Its rows in the authorable-surface, authorable-defaults and api-surface shards and its dropped-refinement entry are untouched by this diff, and its existing tests pass. This is a deviation from the claim's "no change to `RowLevelSecurityPolicySchema` itself", read as "no change to its contract": the `.omit` route the claim names throws, and sharing the rule by name is the alternative to copying it.

## The key and its describe

`defaultRowScope: DefaultRowScopeSchema.optional()`, placed after `sharingModel`. Its describe is published text that SDKs and AI authors read, so it states:

- the shape: a permission set's `rowLevelSecurity` entry without `object`, with `object` refused;
- the four semantics of ruling item 2, as the contract the security plugin's row-policy collection is to meet once it reads the key: the default is to apply when no held set carries a row policy for the object; an authored set policy is to be used as authored; a superuser-bypass principal is to be unaffected; an object without the key keeps its behaviour;
- its writers, by what they are and as what is to happen, since no object declares the key yet: "The platform's identity objects are to declare it for their own tables." (narrowed in patch round 1 from the present-tense "Declared by the platform's identity objects for their own tables."; the changeset, the TSDoc, the liveness note and the form ledger row were narrowed the same way);
- once, plainly: "Not applied yet: no server reads this key in this release, so declaring it filters no rows. Until the collection applies it, restrict rows with a permission set's `rowLevelSecurity` policy."

No tracker number appears in the describe, the guidance or the history sentence (`check:doc-authoring`). The TSDoc beside the key and the schema names the cards.

## What else moves, each by its own tool

- **Liveness ledger** (`packages/spec/liveness/object.json`): `defaultRowScope` is `planned`, with `authorWarn` and an `authorHint`. That is the pending-reader spelling the `action.outcomeMessages` row used: authoring the key raises one `liveness-planned-property` warning (probed: one finding on an object that declares it, zero on the control). The row is drilled into eight `planned` children, because `check:liveness` refuses an undeclared container inheritance, and deferring to `permission/rowLevelSecurity` fails its equality check (the key sets differ by `object`, `priority`, `tags`). Only the container carries `authorWarn`, so the warning fires once. The note gives the flip condition: go `live` on the commit that lands #24340, citing `collectRLSPolicies`, and drop `authorWarn` / `authorHint` in the same edit.
- **Generated artefacts**, all by `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated --fix` after a build: `authorable-surface/{data,security}.json`, `authorable-defaults/security.json`, `json-schema.manifest/security.json`, `api-surface/security.json`, `export-origins/security.json`, `declaration-map/security.json`, `liveness/state-counts/object.md`, the reference pages under `content/docs/references/**`, and the strictness-ledger counts (`docs/audits/2026-07-unknown-key-strictness-ledger.counts/security.md`: one more strict site in `rls.zod.ts`).
- **`dropped-refinements.baseline.json`** (hand-edited by design, no generator): one new entry, `security/DefaultRowScope` at the root, and the new `defaultRowScope` site added to the nine entries that embed `ObjectSchema` (`data/Object`, the three `system/*` change-set shapes and five `api/*` responses), as the build printed them; `measured` moved 239/771 to 240/781, which `dropped-refinements.test.ts` holds equal to the entries. The refinement is the policy's own; it has no JSON Schema form, exactly as on `security/RowLevelSecurityPolicy`, which is already listed.
- **Studio form**: the object form does not offer the key. The root-ledger row in `metadata-form-zod-reconciliation.test.ts` records why: no server applies the key yet, so a form row would let an author declare a row restriction that filters nothing; its writers are to be the platform objects, declared in code, and none declares it yet. Revisit when the reader lands.
- **`composeStacks` with `objectConflict: 'merge'`**: the composer derives the refused fixed-shape config objects from `ObjectSchema.shape`, so it now refuses two stacks that declare a different `defaultRowScope` on one object, like `access` or `publicSharing`, and the refusal text's list of config objects names `defaultRowScope` too. No composition changes today, because no stack declares the key. The two literal lists in `compose-stacks-merge-{collection,config-object}-refusal.test.ts` gained the key in shape order.
- **Field-level-security projection** (`@objectstack/metadata-core`, patch round 2, commit `91b2f39f3`): `OBJECT_REFERENCE_POSITIONS` in `object-schema-fls-references.ts` classifies `defaultRowScope` as one rule entry (`ruleEntry`, the per-entry test `ruleEntries` already applies). When an object document is served to a caller who cannot read some fields, the whole policy is dropped if its `using`, `check` or prose names one of them, and served unchanged otherwise: the `validations` posture, because deleting only `using` would serve a policy that reads as restricting nothing. No behaviour moves until an object declares the key.
- **Served `/meta/types` count** (`@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, same commit): the `object` control in `protocol.meta-types-degenerate-derivation.test.ts` moves 45 to 46, with its history sentence.
- **Changeset** `.changeset/24338-object-default-row-scope.md`: `minor` on `@objectstack/spec` and `patch` on `@objectstack/metadata-core`, with the line `Clause-②: yes (widening)`.

## Tests

`packages/spec/src/data/object-default-row-scope.test.ts`, the card's three cases plus a control:

1. a policy without `object` parses, with `enabled: true` defaulted;
2. a policy carrying `object` is refused: one issue, `unrecognized_keys`, at path `defaultRowScope`, keys `['object']`, and the message carries the implied-object guidance;
3. an unknown key is still refused (`unrecognized_keys`, keys `['appliesTo']`);
4. control: an object without the key parses, and its output has no `defaultRowScope`.

Also: the same through the `object` metadata write door (`getMetadataTypeSchema('object')`); both cross-field rules (no clause: `custom` at `defaultRowScope`; `check` on `select`: `custom` at `defaultRowScope.check`); the tombstoned keys refused as unknown keys; the members are the policy schema's own instances; and the compile-time type equality.

**Ablation (one, on the behaviour this diff adds):** keep `object` in the members, through `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor 1 to 0, blob `b68921414f53` to `26896837459d`). Expected direction red, observed red and wider than the `object` case alone: 8 of 10 failed, because a kept `object` is required, so every scope without it fails. The control and the compile-time case stayed green. Restored: blob equals the HEAD blob `b68921414f53`, and `git diff HEAD` is empty. No build is involved, because the test imports `src` through a relative path.

**Reverse verification of the rebuilt `.d.ts` downstream:** a temporary file in `packages/platform-objects/src` calling `ObjectSchema.create({ …, defaultRowScope: { name, operation: 'select', using } })` typechecks (exit 0). A stale declaration file would refuse the key through `NoExcessObjectKeys`. Appending a second call with `operation: 'nope'` fails with TS2322 at the probe (exit 1). The probe was removed and `git status` is clean.

Patch round 2, on the final head `e254e52d0`, through `os-verify-lock.sh`:

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-core test`: 18 files, 770 tests passed (769 before plus the new pin).
- `protocol.meta-types-degenerate-derivation.test.ts`: 18 passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-core typecheck` (both `tsc` legs): exit 0.
- The new pin in `object-schema-fls-references.test.ts` (commit `e254e52d0`) has three legs. A `using` naming a denied field drops the scope. A `using` naming only readable fields keeps it unchanged. A denied field named like the policy's own schema word `operation` keeps it too, because in a classified position a key is a schema word, not a field reference.
- Ablation of the `ruleEntry` line, two runs through `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`. First run: only the key-coverage test went red, and the pin's first two legs stayed green. The unclassified fail-safe drops on a mention as well, so those legs could not tell the classification from it. That is why the third leg was added. Second run, with it: the pin and the coverage test both red (2 failed, 54 passed). Restored each time: blob equals HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty.

Patch round 1 (describe and TSDoc wording only), on `62170b56e`: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated --fix` rebuilt spec, regenerated `content/docs/references/{data/object,api/metadata,system/migration}.mdx` and re-checked all 14 artefacts green. `object-default-row-scope.test.ts` and `metadata-form-zod-reconciliation.test.ts`: 86 passed. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck`: exit 0. `pnpm check:doc-authoring`: exit 0 (9445 describe strings clean).

Round-0 local runs, on `8964dfbbb` (after merging `origin/main`), through `os-verify-lock.sh`:

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test`: 696 files passed, 21246 tests passed, 1 todo.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck`: exit 0; the test layer compiles with no new errors.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated --fix`: all 14 generated artefacts up to date, measured against a dist built by that run.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run --project repo src/security/rls-tags-retirement.test.ts`: 14 passed (pre-merge head `00929288f`; the merge did not touch it).
- Downstream: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/platform-objects typecheck` exit 0, and 8 `@objectstack/lint` files that read `ObjectSchema.shape` or the liveness ledger: 1191 tests passed.

## Who imports `ObjectSchema` in a way an added optional key could affect

Measured, not assumed. In this repo, `git grep` for `keyof ServiceObject`, `keyof ObjectSchema` and `keyof z.input` of the object schema finds only spec's own `NoExcessObjectKeys`, which an added key widens. The runtime enumerations of `Object.keys(ObjectSchema.shape)` are the two `composeStacks` pins, updated above, and the lint tests above, which stay green. Two more runtime pins enumerate the key set under spellings round 0's search missed, and `Test Core` (5/6, 6/6) went red on them at `8964dfbbb` and `62170b56e`. One is `packages/metadata-core/src/object-schema-fls-references.test.ts` ("classify each new ObjectSchema key in OBJECT_REFERENCE_POSITIONS", which reads `declaredKeys(ObjectSchema)`). The other is `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.meta-types-degenerate-derivation.test.ts` (the served `object` property count). Both are fixed in this PR, in commit `91b2f39f3`: `defaultRowScope` is classified as one rule entry, and the count moves to 46. Commit `e254e52d0` adds the pin beside the classification. The seat extended the claim's file surface to these files in patch round 2. In objectui at the pin, `object-schema-metadata-spec-derivation.test.ts` asserts the document type equals `ServiceObject` plus an empty client delta. That holds structurally for an added optional key, and its runtime half asserts `toContain`, not an exact key count.

The changeset gates are among them: `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-empty-changeset` and `check-adr-0087-registration` against `origin/main`, all exit 0.

- 108 exit 0 on `e254e52d0` (107 of 111 on `8964dfbbb` and on `62170b56e`).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec run check:skill-examples`, `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `pnpm check:lean-entry-closure`: exit 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET. They need built `client-react`, every package's `dist`, and `objectql`'s `dist`, which this worktree does not have. NOT MEASURED, and left to CI.
- `pnpm check:platform-checklist`: exit 1, and not from this diff. `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/access-security.json:2823` cites `packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts#legacyGrantAnchorRetired`, a symbol that file does not declare at `origin/main` (nor at the base `b2e78701f7`). This diff touches neither file. By maintainer decision the gate is not in per-PR CI (`lint.yml` note), and its daily watchdog on `main` is the reporting channel.
- `pnpm check:dev-prereqs` (local-only family): exit 0.

## Acceptance notes

- **Open question for the declarations card #24341.** Under the ruled single-policy key, `sys_user`'s two shipped literals (`sys_user_self`, `id == current_user.id`, and `sys_user_org_members`, `id in current_user.org_user_ids`, in `default-permission-sets.ts`) cannot both move unrewritten, which that card's text asks. One `||` policy is row-equivalent wherever `org_user_ids` resolves to an array, which the core resolver always produces (`resolve-authz-context.ts` seeds `[]` / `[userId]`). But the compiler drops a whole policy on any unresolved variable. Measured with `compileCelToFilter` (`@objectstack/formula` source): with `org_user_ids` unresolved, the merged predicate is refused `unresolved-variable`, while `id == current_user.id` alone compiles to `{ id: 'u1' }`; with `org_user_ids: []` the merged predicate compiles to an `$or` of the two arms. So for an execution context built without `org_user_ids`, the merged policy loses the self arm, which two separate policies keep. Explain would also name one policy, not two. Details are in the dev report on #24338. The seat answered A in `6255131226`: this PR keeps the single-policy shape.
- **The authoring-time predicate checks cover permission-set policies only.** `validate-rls-predicate-enforceability.ts` walks `permissions[].rowLevelSecurity`, so a `defaultRowScope.using` that does not lower is not refused at authoring time. Today that has no effect, because nothing reads the key. Carrier: #24340, before the reader applies the key.
- `validate-org-axis-red-lines.test.ts` is titled "object-level RLS is not an authoring surface" and asserts that `ObjectSchema` declares neither `rowLevelSecurity` nor `rls`. It stays green, but its title is now only true of those two spellings.
